targetAudience.primary: Agent-platform, multi-agent protocol and human-authorization architects
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands human-in-the-loop tool approval and message relays such as A2A and HTTP.
targetAudience.readerProblem: An approval can travel through several channels, but transport metadata and user-shaped message roles do not identify the human principal authorized to approve the exact action.

whyNow: A same-day Google ADK revert removed an A2A-metadata confirmation guard because it blocked legitimate relayed approvals while leaving equivalent approval ingress elsewhere; the underlying issue was explicitly reopened without a replacement principal-binding mechanism.

externalHook.description: A security guard correctly identifies a channel but answers the wrong authorization question and must be reverted.

coreProposition: Human approval in agent systems should be a principal-bound authorization object that binds the authenticated approver, exact pending action, scope or policy, and freshness or replay boundary; transport provenance is supporting risk context rather than authority, and the ADK revert leaves the replacement mechanism unresolved.

originalValue.description: Turns the failure of transport gating into a concrete authorization record that separates channel, principal, pending action, scope and freshness.

readerTakeaway: Use transport as contextual evidence, authenticate the approving principal end to end, bind approval to the exact pending effect and prevent replay; do not treat a revert as a completed security fix.

supported: The selected ADK commit reverts an A2A-metadata confirmation guard and reopens the issue.
The reporter describes A2A and HTTP paths for confirmation-shaped input.
The reverted guard rejected confirmation based on transport metadata and did not address other ingress.
The selected revert adds no replacement principal identifier, credential, signature or verifier in the shown path.
unsupported: That the reported exploit was independently reproduced here
That all ADK deployments expose unauthenticated ingress
That the revert solves human-approval authorization
That one specific replacement design has been selected by maintainers
uncertain: Which principal representation should survive every supported relay
How pending actions and approval freshness will be bound in a future implementation

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general authorization architecture for agent systems and does not rely on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The revert, issue and prior mitigation expose a concrete trust-proxy failure, and the Research Object derives a bounded authorization contract without claiming an unimplemented fix.
